title: Refuse jj operation-log rewrites (undo / abandon / op restore|revert|abandon|undo) in every phase-worker pane

decisionsNeeded.question: Should the guard also bind a phase worker's in-process `task` subagents?
decisionsNeeded.currentState: legion.ts:597-600 returns before any gate for a subagent session (`if (await checkSubagentSession(context)) return undefined;`), on the reasoning that the parent's own gate governed the parent's `task` call. That holds for edit/write, not for this guard: the parent's `task` call carries a prompt, the subagent's bash carries the `jj undo`, and it runs in the same pane against the same shared operation log. The spec scopes Acceptance 1–5 to bash/eval/hub in the phase-worker branch and says nothing about subagents; this plan implements exactly that scope.
options: A (spec as written, planned below): guard inside the phase-worker branch only; a scout/reviewer subagent spawned by a worker can still run `jj undo`.

B (recommended): additionally evaluate the guard before the subagent early return whenever the pane's environment classifies as a phase worker — `classifySession(process.env).kind === "phase-worker"`, computed once per module instance on first tool_call (never at module load: the tests set env before calling legionExtension, but a throw for an unrecognised LEGION_ROLE must stay inside the handler). Roughly 8 lines: hoist the `jjAttempt` check to run right after the debug log when that classification holds, and drop the copy inside the branch. One extra test: boot as in 'never bootstraps, claims a role, or exits for a subagent session, even with phase-worker environment' (legion.test.ts:1258) and assert a bash `jj undo` from the subagent context is refused with the shared-log reason while `legion state` still passes.
decisionsNeeded.recommendation: B. Same blast radius, same fix, one pane; the spec's own argument for covering eval and hub ('refusing only bash would leave the problem in the title true') applies verbatim. It changes a documented invariant ('No gate of any kind applies to a subagent's own tool calls'), so it is the architect's call and a spec amendment (Acceptance 6), not a silent widening.
decisionsNeeded.whoDecides: architect (spec owner) before spawning the implementer; the implementer applies B as an extra step 1b if approved.

newSinceSpec: Quoted shell words are opaque to the tokenizer but each is still held to the plain-text rule, so `sh -c 'jj undo'`, `bash -lc "jj op restore x"`, and a heredoc/echo containing `jj undo` are refused (spec Errors row 'never allow by default' applied to nested shells). Cost: a commit message or PR body that mentions `jj undo` cannot be written through bash text; the skill paragraph tells workers to use the write tool or say 'operation-log rollback'.

'Bare' means at least one character of the word was unquoted and unescaped: `"undo"` and `'undo'` are message words; `un"do"` and `un\do` are the subcommand. `jj describe -m "undo"` (single quoted word) is therefore allowed, `jj describe -m undo` refused — exactly the spec's 'unquoted message word' line.

hub: `text` (stdin sent to a supervised process with `op: send`) is judged alongside `application` and `args`, since a supervised shell would run it; regardless of `op`, so the check is one join. Reversible by deleting one array element.

The refusal names the offending invocation as its unquoted words (`jj -R $LEGION_WORKSPACE undo`) for bash, and `<tool>: jj <words>` (`eval: jj op restore`, `hub: jj undo`) for the plain-text rule. Tests assert the three required contents (command name, 'every Legion issue workspace shares', recovery: 'new commit' + 'jj restore <paths>' + 'architect') with stringContaining, never the exact sentence.

The plain-text regex allows any non-word run between op/operation and restore/revert (`\b(?:op|operation)\b\W+(?:restore|revert)\b`) so an argv literal `["jj", "op", "restore"]` in eval code counts; `jj op log; jj restore f` does not (word characters intervene). Case-sensitive: the subcommands are lowercase and that is the threat.

A refused command also never mints a grant (the guard returns before the grant path at legion.ts:648+); step 1's test pins it — a wrongly minted 60-second grant would be a live credential for a command that never ran.

Step 6 adds `--prompt-file` to the grant rig (packages/pi-envoy/scripts/grant-rig/run.ts) so the tester can drive a real production-profile worker through the refused and allowed commands and read the real op log — the production-like surface Sami requires (legion-worker skill, 2026-09-13 ruling). Without it there is no surface: the rig's prompt is hard-coded.

Commit messages and test names in this plan avoid putting `jj` and a blocked word in one quoted argument, so they remain typeable through bash once this guard is deployed to the panes that will maintain it.

decisions.decision: Four unexported functions and five module constants in legion.ts directly after isSingleLegionCommand (line 167) and before LEGION_LOADED_MARKER (line 174): jjLogRewriteMention, splitShellCommands (+ interface ShellWord), jjLogRewriteInvocation, jjLogRewriteAttempt. isSingleLegionCommand is not modified. Static word tables are string arrays with .includes (matches CODE_MUTATION_TOOLS; project rule ts-set-map).

Inside `if (active?.kind === "phase-worker") { … }` (legion.ts:629-647), after the merger check and before the closing brace. Consequences pinned by tests: root architect (kind root-architect) and controller (no capability, LEGION_CONTROLLER=1) never reach it; a sub-architect (phase-worker with role architect) is answered first by the blanket architect bash gate at :609; reviewer and merger bash falls through their tool checks to the guard; a refused call returns before the grant is minted.

Per simple command, the first bare word equal to `jj` or ending in `/jj` starts the invocation; its bare arguments are refused when any equals undo/abandon, or when one equals op/operation and another equals restore/revert (order-insensitive; whole list, so global options before the subcommand do not matter). Separators: ; & | newline ( ) backtick outside quotes — `&&`, `||`, `$(…)`, subshells, and backticks all fall out of that.
Unterminated quote → plain-text rule on the whole command. Quoted word → plain-text rule on the word. Neither ever allows on failure to parse (spec Errors row).

code:
**Shared operation safety:** Every Legion issue workspace is a `jj workspace` of one shared
clone, so they all share one operation log: `jj undo`, `jj abandon`, and
`jj op restore|revert|abandon|undo` rewrite it for every tree at once (on 2026-09-12 one
worker's `jj undo` rewrote nine of another tree's commits). The extension refuses them in every
phase-worker pane before they run — a `bash` command in any position of a pipeline or `&&`
chain, with or without `-R`, judged on the whole argument list; `eval` code; and a `hub`
process start — and a `bash` command whose quoted text merely mentions `jj` with one of those
words (a heredoc, an echo, a commit message) is refused too: write such text with the `write`
tool or say "operation-log rollback" instead. `jj restore <paths>`, `jj op log`, and
`jj op show` stay allowed. Recover forward only: a new commit (`jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" new`)
or `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" restore <paths>` of files. Anything else, stop and send the
owning architect the `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" log` evidence; the architect decides, and an
operator performs any operation-log restore with every other tree paused.
